newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Austrim races higher after profit surge.
newsitem.headline: Austrim races higher after profit surge.

text.p: Shares in investment group Austrim Ltd jumped 45 cents or almost 12 percent to A$4.25 in Monday morning trade after announcing a sharp rise in annual profit and a rights issue to retire debt.
Austrim said it planned a two-for-five rights issue at A$3.30 a share to raise A$208 million.
Austrim reported a net profit of A$21.9 million for the year to June 30, up from A$4.4 million the previous year and increased its final dividend to 5.5 cents per share from two cents per share.
Sales rose to A$156.7 million from A$5.1 million.
This higher profit was due largely to a heavy acquisition programme during 1996/97, which totalled A$178.1 million.
Brokers had expected an annual profit of about A$15 million to A$18 million and were not surprised to see the rights issue, which Austrim flagged in June.
Brokers said investors were happy with the profit result and confident company founder Alan Jackson, former chief executive of BTR Plc, would continue the group's profitable expansion.
"The better than expected profit shows that Alan Jackson has put together a pretty dynamic group," said Burdett, Buckeridge and Young's Graham Buckeridge.
Buckeridge said investors were buying into Jackson's vision of buying unspectacular industrial assets at reasonable prices and creating leverage by putting them together.
"It's a continuation of his philosophy at BTR," Buckeridge said.
Austrim Chairman Jackson said in a statement released with the results the group was confident of further growth in 1997/98.

Austrim, which is not widely analysed, was expected before these results to boost profits to as much as A$27 million in 1997/98, raising earnings per share to about 17 cents a share from the actual 16.6 cents a share reported for 1996/97.
Austrim was trading at a price to expected earnings ratio of about 24 in late morning trade, well above other Australian industrials.
